stages.title: Bare Cell
stages.notes: The minimum board, zero terrain — the pure-duel control and the smallest arena the trigger can draw. Deliberately untouched by furniture.

stages.title: Cluttered Closet
stages.notes: Smallest crate fight: two pieces of furniture on otherwise open minimum-width ground. Every capture-the-clutter line is worth a tempo question even at 3 files.

stages.title: The Pantry
stages.notes: Small mixed ground: one stone pillar among shelves of clutter, packed toward midfield so both armies still deploy. First taste of stone-vs-furniture reading at a glance.

stages.title: Barrel Row
stages.notes: A broken furniture line across midfield, no stone at all. The stone-only control arm of this stage is an open field — the crates ARE the terrain.

stages.title: The Squeeze
stages.notes: Stone waist leaving a 2-wide pass, with one crate narrowing it further — pay a capture to widen the pass, or file through under fire.

stages.title: Crate Court
stages.notes: Pillared court with loose clutter: two stone pillars, four crates. Baseline mixed-density middle-size arena.

stages.title: The Doorway
stages.notes: A full wall with a 2-wide door — one leaf open, one leaf furniture. Smash the door for the wide file or funnel through the open half.

stages.title: Storeroom
stages.notes: One-sided clutter: five crates crowd one deployment approach, the other is clean. Asymmetric by design — the flip convention tests it facing each side.

stages.title: Long Gallery
stages.notes: Narrow-tall pure-stone gallery, staggered pillars. The stone-only reference point among the tall boards — no furniture on purpose.

stages.title: Broken Barricade
stages.notes: A furniture barricade spanning the field between stone end-stubs, one open gap. Fight for the gap or smash a second one — the engine prices both.

stages.title: Grand Hall
stages.notes: The big open hall: three stone pillars, five scattered furnishings. Light terrain at maximum size — long diagonals still live here.

stages.title: Rat Nest
stages.notes: Density stress: dense mixed pockets of stone and clutter, including one crate in each deployment approach. The generator must still deal every army width here.

stages.title: Gatehouse
stages.notes: Stone stubs in BOTH back ranks with a furniture gate-leaf beside each. Crates on the king rows are capture-promotion squares (§4.6) — march a pawn and smash in.

stages.title: Weak Wall
stages.notes: A full-width stone wall whose only ways through are two furniture breaches. Furniture alone separates the armies — legal (§4.6), the verifier flags it: you MUST smash in.

stages.title: Colonnade
stages.notes: Pillar pairs with furniture stacked between them — the colonnade reads solid until somebody starts clearing the shelving.

stages.title: Cave Mouth
stages.notes: The near back rank is rock except a 1-square mouth and a weak-masonry plug. The king molds into the mouth; the enemy can capture-promote onto the plug.

stages.title: Rubble Yard
stages.notes: Mixed stone-and-crate rubble strictly in midfield, deployment rows clean. The workhorse mixed-density case for the corpus.

stages.title: Split Cellars
stages.notes: Stone spurs split both deployment areas into cellar pockets; crates sit where a door would be. Molding pours armies around the spurs.

stages.title: Diagonal Scar
stages.notes: A broken diagonal alternating stone and furniture. The scar can be partially reopened — every second segment is smashable.

stages.title: The Anvil
stages.notes: Mirrored materials: stone pair on one side's second rank, crate pair on the other's. Same shape, different permanence — the cleanest A/B of wall vs furniture in deployment.

stages.title: Collapsed Keep
stages.notes: Big-board stress: rubble in both deployment zones, room walls midfield, loose crates in the wreckage. The 10x10 everything-at-once case.

stages.title: Sinkhole
stages.notes: A 2x2 stone sink with furniture heaped on its flanks — the hole is forever, the heap is not.

stages.title: The Neck
stages.notes: Room-corridor-room with offset throats sharing one furniture column. The only stone-open cells are NOT adjacent — clearing the crate column is the fast route. Verifier-flagged smash-in (§4.6).

stages.title: Hypostyle
stages.notes: Alternating pillar lattice — half the pillars are stone, half furniture. The lattice thins as the duel burns through it.

stages.title: The Divide
stages.notes: A full central spine with two corridors — except one spine cell is furniture. Route A: the corridor. Route B: make your own door.

stages.title: Flats
stages.notes: Wide-shallow ground with only light clutter and no stone. Wide flanks, short files — the cavalry board.

stages.title: Posterngate
stages.notes: Both back ranks walled except opposite-corner gates — one leaf open, one furniture. Kings mold into the gates; the auto-crop and camp lines earn their keep here.

stages.title: Parapet
stages.notes: The near second rank is a parapet with one open slot and one weak slot — pawns deploy DEEP, and the camp line sits forward of the king row.

stages.title: The Redoubt
stages.notes: A sealed corner chamber in the far side's territory whose only door is furniture. Sometimes the defender molds INTO it — a fortress with a capturable door is the §4.6 thesis stage.

stages.title: The Serpent
stages.notes: S-weave of stone arms with crates at two bends. The long way is safe; the short way is bought with captures.

stages.title: Ruined L
stages.notes: A solid collapsed quadrant makes an L-shaped playfield; two weak-masonry cells on the ruin's edge can be dug out for nooks.

stages.title: Smugglers' Hold
stages.notes: Three-wide staggered passes, one plugged with contraband. Knife-fight geometry at minimum width.

stages.title: The Vault
stages.notes: The minimum square: one crate, one pillar, gap 1. The smallest board where stone and furniture coexist.

stages.title: Double Doors
stages.notes: The requested archetype, plain: one full wall, one ^^ double door, no other way through. Furniture alone joins the halves — the verifier flags it; you smash in.

stages.title: The Antechamber
stages.notes: Two partitions in sequence: an open door into the antechamber, then a ^^ double door into the far hall. Room-corridor-room the way a generator would draw it.

stages.title: Crate Hoard
stages.notes: A holed corner room with the hoard inside — and now a breakable floor-edge (c5, d5) so the room can be cracked open from below as well as entered through the gap. Designer tweak 2026-08-27.

stages.title: Twin Vaults
stages.notes: A full-height spine splits the field into two vaults — one open hole, one weak point — with a crate cluster stored in each half. Two sub-battles, three ways to merge them.

stages.title: Quartered
stages.notes: A cross of walls cuts the board into four rooms. Two passages are open holes, two are weak points — the generator's room-graph made literal.

stages.title: The Vestibule
stages.notes: A sealed central chamber with ^^ double doors facing BOTH armies. Take the flanks around it, or smash into the middle and hold the room.

stages.title: Broken Cloister
stages.notes: A solid garden block with clutter heaped at its four bends — the ring corridor narrows to single files exactly where the crates sit.

stages.title: Supply Line
stages.notes: A full wall with one ^^ double door, and supply crates stacked AGAINST the wall on both sides. Furniture integrated into the wall structure; the door is the only way through.

stages.title: Guardroom
stages.notes: Three rooms in a row. One door is open, one is weak — and the weak one has a crate shoved behind it as a barricade. Wide-shallow room-graph with clean deployment rows.

stages.title: The Breach
stages.notes: A castle wall two ranks thick. The breach column is rubble-choked — and the collapse spilled forward: d5 joins the breach and d6 lies in the approach. Smash a path, or smash a wider one. Designer tweak 2026-08-27.

stages.title: Double Gatehouse
stages.notes: One wall, TWO ^^ double doors at the thirds, nothing open. Pick a gate — or price both and let the engine tell you which.

stages.title: Collapsed Arch
stages.notes: A wall whose arch came down: a 3-wide rubble cluster IN the wall itself, plus one intact slip at the edge. Clear the rubble for the broad front or file through the slip.

stages.title: Cellar Steps
stages.notes: A tiny sealed cellar in the near corner — stone on two sides, a weak ceiling slab, a crate on the stairs. Molding can put your own pieces inside; someone has to dig them out.

stages.title: The Warrens
stages.notes: Two full walls and an offset divider, now multiply breached: two weak points per wall and a breakable stub on the divider — every route is a smash, and there are many routes. Verifier-flagged. Designer tweak 2026-08-27.

stages.title: Barricaded Bridge
stages.notes: Stone flanks force everything over a center bridge, and the bridge is half-blocked by a two-crate barricade. One open file under fire, or clear the barricade.

stages.title: Crate Quarry
stages.notes: Clusters only, no stone: a 2x2 block, a 1x3 run, a 2x1 pair. The pure-cluster control — its stone-only arm is an empty field.

stages.title: Last Stand
stages.notes: The redoubt evolved: a far-side pocket with a ^^ double door AND a crate shoring it from inside — three smashes through the center, or come around the flank files.

stages.title: The Corridor
stages.notes: FLOORPLAN: a full-width hallway with two rooms off each side — five areas. Each wall has an open door and a weak door; the room pairs also connect to each other through breakable party doors (e8, f1). NW stocks a crate pair, NE one against the wall, SE an L of three, SW stands bare.

stages.title: The Apartments
stages.notes: FLOORPLAN: three rooms upstairs, two down, six doors — every room reachable two ways, party doors between neighbours (d7, g8, e2). Furnishings differ room to room: a wardrobe pair, a lone chest, a corner stack, a bare parlor.

stages.title: The Cellblock
stages.notes: FLOORPLAN: a central hallway with three cells off each side — seven areas. Left doors are all breakable; right doors alternate open and weak. Some cells hold contraband, some are swept bare.

stages.title: Banquet & Kitchens
stages.notes: FLOORPLAN: a great hall dominated by a four-crate banquet table, and three kitchens behind a wall with a double door and a weak service hatch. The kitchens connect to each other (d7 breakable, g7 open), each stocked differently.

stages.title: Gate & Bailey
stages.notes: FLOORPLAN: an outer wall with a double gate and an open postern, a bailey with stabled crates along the west wall, and a stone keep with one weak door — which the defender may mold inside. Three zones deep.

stages.title: The Archive
stages.notes: FLOORPLAN: two long shelf-rows make three aisles in the stacks; the reading room behind the double door is the only way to the far side (verifier-flagged smash-in), and an inner cage with its own weak door guards the rarest holdings.

stages.title: Crossroads Market
stages.notes: FLOORPLAN: two hallways cross at an open square, with an L-walled stall in each quadrant — five areas, every stall door different (two weak, two placements), every stall stocked differently: one chest, a pair, a spill of three, one empty.

stages.title: Drowned Halls
stages.notes: FLOORPLAN: the dense one — six areas. Two full walls with mixed doors bracket a mid band split into three chambers by dividers with party doors (d4, g5); the north territory splits again behind a weak door. Flooded chambers hold flotsam; the center hall is scoured bare.
